New Year's Day: The First Ride

For many UK motorcyclists, the year doesn't truly begin until you've swung a leg over the bike and turned the key. The New Year's Day first ride is a tradition as old as motorcycling itself — symbolic, restorative, and the perfect way to blow away the holiday cobwebs.

The Tradition

The rules are simple: ride your motorcycle on January 1st. That's it. Whether it's a 5-mile loop of the neighbourhood or a 100-mile blast to a biker café, the first ride of the year carries a special significance.

  • Some riders maintain a log of their first-ride destination each year
  • Some have a specific first-ride route they repeat annually
  • Many clubs organise group first rides with a café or pub destination
  • Some riders set a distance target for the year and start counting from their first ride

Popular New Year Meets

  • Ace Café, London: A legendary gathering point. New Year's Day sees hundreds of bikes converge.
  • Squires Café, Sherburn in Elmet: One of the UK's most famous biker cafés hosts a New Year meet.
  • Box Hill, Surrey: A classic meeting point for London-area riders on New Year's Day.
  • Matlock Bath, Derbyshire: The Peak District's biker honeypot draws crowds even on January 1st.

Safety on New Year's Day

  • Check road conditions carefully — New Year's Day can bring ice, frost, or snow.
  • Ride only if conditions are safe. The tradition isn't worth a crash.
  • Be alert for other road users who may still be affected by New Year's Eve celebrations.
  • Ride sober (obviously) and well-rested.
  • Dress for the worst winter conditions — heated grips, thermal layers, waterproofs.

New Year Riding Resolutions

January 1st is a natural time to set riding goals:

  • Plan the year's touring — which tours, which months, which destinations
  • Set a maintenance schedule for the year
  • Commit to an advanced riding course (IAM, RoSPA)
  • Target new roads or regions you haven't explored
  • Resolve to ride more — it's always a good resolution
The first ride of the year matters because it's a renewal of commitment. Turning the key on January 1st says: I'm a motorcyclist, this is who I am, and this year will be filled with riding. It's the best resolution you'll keep.

Making It Meaningful

Elevate your first ride of the year from a routine quick loop to a genuinely memorable experience. Choose a destination that holds personal significance — the café where you planned your very first motorcycle tour, the viewpoint where you proposed, or the quiet road where you first learned to ride with confidence. Ritual and meaningful repetition give the New Year ride significance that transcends simple mileage accumulation.

Document your first ride with photographs. A picture of your motorcycle on January 1st each year creates a compelling visual diary of your riding life — changing bikes, evolving gear, the same beloved roads captured in different winter conditions. After a few years, these annual photographs become a treasured record of your motorcycling journey through time. If you ride with close friends, make the New Year ride a shared group tradition. A regular crew, a familiar favourite route, and a reliable finish at the same welcoming pub creates layers of shared history and strengthens friendships built upon a common passion for two-wheeled adventure.
